blocks.text: "Beware of asking, 'What is your opinion? What is your opinion?' because those before you were destroyed because they asked, 'What is you opinion? What is you opinion?' You should also not judge one thing by another because your feet will then slip after being firm. In addition to this, whenever any of you are asked about something that he does not know, he should say, 'Allaah knows best,' because this constitutes a third of knowledge." [^1]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once said, "Every year is followed by a year that is worse. While no year is essentially worse than another, no nation is essentially worse than another. However, what will happen is that when your Ulema and righteous ones leave the world, such people will come about who will analyse matters using their personal opinions, because of which they will destroy and perforate Islaam." [^2]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said, "The basis (of Islaam and the Shari'ah) is Allaah's Book and the Sunnah of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Whoever says anything else based on his personal opinion, I cannot say whether he will find this amongst his good deeds or his sins." [^3]

Hadhrat Ataa narrates from his father that when a Sahabi (RA) was questioned about something, he said, "I am too shy before my Rabb to employ my personal opinion in commenting on a matter that affects the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ." [^4]
Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) Tells Rasulullaah ﷺ that he will Practise Ijtihaad without Compromising on Diligence

Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent him to Yemen, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "How will you pass judgement when a case comes before you?" "I shall pass judgement by Allaah's Book," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further, "And what if you do not find the solution in the Book of Allaah?" "Then," Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "I shall judge by the Sunnah of Allaah's Rasool ﷺ." Again Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "And what if you do not find the solution in the Sunnah of Allaah's Rasool ﷺ?" Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) replied by saying, "I shall then practise Ijtihaad without compromising on diligence." Rasulullaah ﷺ then placed his hand on Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA)'s chest saying, "All praise belongs to Allaah Who has inspired the envoy of Rasulullaah ﷺ with that which pleases Rasulullaah

Ijtihaad briefly refers to applying one's mind to the source references of the Shari'ah to extract laws that are not explicitly stated. This is, of course, the work of a person whose proficiency in Islaamic jurisprudence in unquestionable.
